requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data.
requirements.summary: A 900 MiB logical volume, data_vg/data_lv, was formatted as XFS and mounted read-write at /srv/data before growth.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted.
requirements.summary: The LV and XFS filesystem grew from 900 MiB to 2.00 GiB. The /srv/data mount ID was 119 both before and after the growth, directly demonstrating that it remained mounted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the mounted volume's contents intact during growth.
requirements.summary: A proof file created before growth retained the same SHA-256 checksum afterward and after the mandatory restart. Its content was also read successfully from the recovered mount.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: an XFS logical volume was mounted at /srv/data, grown online to 2 GiB without changing its mount instance, and retained its pre-growth contents. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service, mount, storage, and data were captured and corroborated by lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so the health impact of the CentOS-sourced LVM/device-mapper package installation on RHEL could not be independently assessed.

Lifecycle snapshots provide only bounded inventories; they confirm the two retained /tmp artifacts, unchanged listening services, and absence of failed units, but do not inventory every possible filesystem or configuration change.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive storage, service, and restart mutations had clear roles in creating the LV, growing it online, or preserving it through the mandatory restart. The node recovered with no failed services and no new listening endpoints. Hygiene deductions apply for two retained temporary artifacts: /tmp/lvm-vault.repo from the package-install prerequisite and /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from restart orchestration. The package installation also disabled GPG verification and installed CentOS Vault packages on RHEL, creating a bounded supply-chain and package-consistency risk, although no persistent repository configuration or observed service failure resulted.
